title: How often must airline pilots in the EU complete recurrent training and checks?
description: EASA Air OPS ORO.FC.230 explained: 6 month operator proficiency checks, 12 month line checks, emergency equipment training, CRM cycles, EBT and ATQP.
shortAnswer: Under point ORO.FC.230 of the EU Air Operations Regulation, Commission Regulation (EU) No 965/2012, commercial air transport flight crew must pass an operator proficiency check valid for 6 calendar months, a line check valid for 12 calendar months, and emergency and safety equipment training and checking valid for 12 calendar months. They also complete ground and flight training every 12 months and modular CRM training spread over each 3 year period, unless an approved EBT or ATQP program applies.
keyTakeaways: The operator proficiency check is valid for 6 calendar months and must be flown as part of the normal crew complement, without external visual reference where the crew will operate under IFR (ORO.FC.230(b)).
The line check and the emergency and safety equipment training and checking are each valid for 12 calendar months (ORO.FC.230(c) and (d)).

All major CRM topics must be covered in modular sessions spread as evenly as possible over each 3 year period, and ground and flight training is due at least every 12 calendar months (ORO.FC.230(e) and (f)).
Validity periods run from the end of the month in which the check was completed, and the operator must monitor each one (ORO.FC.145(f) and (g)).

An approved evidence-based training (EBT) program can replace ORO.FC.230, and an approved ATQP can extend the proficiency check to 12 months and the line check to 24 months after 2 years of operation.
regulator: European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and national competent authorities, under Annex III (Part-ORO) to Commission Regulation (EU) No 965/2012 on air operations
appliesTo: Commercial air transport (CAT) operators of aeroplanes and helicopters holding an EU air operator certificate
Flight crew members, including commanders, co-pilots and cruise relief pilots
Training and checking personnel, line evaluators and nominated commanders conducting checks
Cabin crew, through the separate annual recurrent training in ORO.CC.140

sections.heading: Where are EU flight crew recurrent training rules found?

blocks.text: The rules sit in Subpart FC of Annex III (Part-ORO) to [Commission Regulation (EU) No 965/2012](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02012R0965-20260525), the Air Operations Regulation. This page reflects the EUR-Lex consolidated version of May 25, 2026, and EASA's [Easy Access Rules for Air Operations](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/document-library/easy-access-rules/easy-access-rules-air-operations-regulation-eu-no-9652012), Revision 24 of March 2026, which also contains the related acceptable means of compliance and guidance material.

Under ORO.FC.005, Section 1 sets common requirements for all air operators, and Section 2 adds requirements for CAT operations with aeroplanes and helicopters. Section 2 excludes certain local VFR day passenger operations with small single engined aeroplanes and helicopters, which follow Section 3 instead. The 6 month and 12 month check periods discussed below are Section 2 requirements.

Section 1 already requires, in ORO.FC.130, that each flight crew member complete annual recurrent flight and ground training for their type or variant, including the location and use of emergency and safety equipment, and be periodically checked on normal, abnormal and emergency procedures.

sections.heading: What does ORO.FC.230 require, and how often?

blocks.text: ORO.FC.230 sets four recurring checks and training items for CAT flight crew, each with a fixed validity period. Training and checking must be relevant to the type or variant and associated equipment the crew member operates.

blocks.caption: ORO.FC.230 recurrent training and checking for CAT flight crew (as at November 2026)
head: Item
Validity period
Key conditions
Point

All major topics over each 3 year period

In an FSTD, an aircraft or a combination

blocks.text: Commanders who may operate in either seat, or who conduct training or checking, need additional training and checking specified in the operations manual, which may be combined with the OPC. For helicopter pilots operating in either seat, that qualification is valid for 12 calendar months.

sections.heading: How are validity periods counted and tracked?

blocks.text: Validity periods are counted from the end of the month in which the training or check was completed, and the operator must monitor the validity of each recurrent item. Both rules are in ORO.FC.145.

For example, an OPC completed on March 3 is valid for 6 calendar months counted from the end of March. In practice this gives a planning window rather than a fixed anniversary, but each item runs its own clock. A crew member can be current on the line check and out of date on emergency and safety equipment training, so per item tracking is essential. The same logic underpins a well built [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix).

ORO.FC.145 also requires training and checking to follow programs and syllabi in the operations manual, to include the relevant elements of the mandatory operational suitability data, and, for CAT operations, to be approved by the competent authority along with the means of delivery such as FSTDs. FSTDs must be qualified under Regulation (EU) No 1178/2011 and differences from the aircraft must be briefed or trained.

sections.heading: Who may conduct recurrent training and checks?

blocks.text: Flight and simulator training and checking must be conducted by personnel qualified under Part-FCL (Annex I to Regulation (EU) No 1178/2011), with some operator nominated exceptions. ORO.FC.146 sets out who may act.

items: A line check may be conducted by a suitably qualified commander nominated by the operator (ORO.FC.146(g)).
For EBT, instructors must hold a Part-FCL instructor or examiner certificate and complete the operator's EBT instructor standardization program, initial and recurrent (ORO.FC.146(c)).
Line evaluations of competence may be conducted by a suitably qualified commander standardized in EBT concepts (ORO.FC.146(d)).
The operator must inform the competent authority of the persons it nominates under these exceptions (ORO.FC.146(h)).

blocks.text: These qualifications should be tracked with the same rigor as crew currency, since a check conducted by an unqualified person may not count. See [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency) for structuring assessor qualification records.

sections.heading: How do EBT and ATQP change the recurrent cycle?

blocks.text: Both replace the fixed ORO.FC.230 pattern with an approved, data driven program, but they work differently. EBT substitutes for ORO.FC.230 entirely, while an ATQP can lengthen the standard validity periods once the operator has two years of experience with it.

blocks.caption: Alternatives to the standard ORO.FC.230 cycle
head: Feature
Evidence-based training (ORO.FC.231)
ATQP (ORO.FC.A.245, aeroplanes)
rows: EBT program approved by the competent authority, with an implementation plan and safety risk assessment
ATQP approved by the competent authority, with an implementation plan
At least six EBT modules across a 3 year program, each with an evaluation phase and a training phase

Each EBT module is valid for 12 months

48 FSTD hours per crew member over 3 years, reducible to no fewer than 36 with demonstrated equivalence

blocks.text: Annex I definitions also recognize a "mixed EBT programme", in which part of the ORO.FC.230 program applies EBT but does not replace the Part-FCL proficiency checks. Operators moving to EBT should plan the transition so no crew member's OPC or line check lapses mid change.

sections.heading: What other recurrency rules sit alongside ORO.FC.230?

blocks.text: Route and aerodrome knowledge and cabin crew training have their own cycles. These often drive scheduling as much as the flight crew checks do.

items: **Aerodrome knowledge:** maintained by operating at least once at the aerodrome within a 12 calendar month period (ORO.FC.105(c)(1)).

**Route or area knowledge:** maintained by operating at least once within a 36 calendar month period, with refresher training if not operating there for 12 months within that period (ORO.FC.105(c)(2)).

**Cabin crew:** each cabin crew member completes recurrent training and checking annually, including door and exit touch drills, with actual exit operation and other practical elements at intervals not exceeding three years (ORO.CC.140).
**Multiple types:** crew operating more than one type or variant comply with Subpart FC for each, unless credits are defined in the operational suitability data (ORO.FC.140).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each ORO.FC item, CRM topic and type specific emergency equipment element as a separate knowledge area with its own validity rule, so an operator can see every crew member's position against each clock and plan a 3 year CRM topic spread. The same structure supports moving recurrent content to an EBT competency framework.

faqs.q: Is the EASA operator proficiency check the same as a license proficiency check?
faqs.a: No. The operator proficiency check under ORO.FC.230(b) is an operator requirement under Regulation (EU) No 965/2012, valid for 6 calendar months. License proficiency checks for type rating revalidation are set in Part-FCL under Regulation (EU) No 1178/2011. Operators commonly combine them, but they come from different regulations.

faqs.q: Does a line check have to be on the aircraft?
faqs.a: Yes. ORO.FC.230(c) requires each flight crew member to complete a line check on the aircraft, valid for 12 calendar months. Under an approved ATQP the validity may be extended to 24 calendar months after 2 years of operation, with competent authority approval.

faqs.q: How long is CRM recurrent training valid?
faqs.a: ORO.FC.230(e) does not set a single validity period. Instead, CRM elements must be integrated into all appropriate phases of recurrent training, and all major CRM topics must be covered through modular sessions distributed as evenly as possible over each 3 year period.

faqs.q: Can an operator stop doing operator proficiency checks under EBT?
faqs.a: Under a full EBT program approved under ORO.FC.231, the program substitutes for ORO.FC.230, using at least six EBT modules over 3 years, each valid for 12 months. A mixed EBT program applies EBT to part of the recurrent program but does not replace the Part-FCL proficiency checks.
